In May 2024, due to repeated episodes of CHF exacerbation, vericiguat was initiated at 2.5 mg once daily. At the time of initiation, he had a low-normal systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 105 mmHg and a normal heart rate. Renal function and blood pressure were monitored every 2-4 weeks during follow-up. After three months of therapy, he demonstrated marked clinical improvement, with resolution of dyspnea and only mild leg swelling noted. He had no further hospitalizations during this period, and repeat TTE showed an increase in LVEF to 30%. Renal function (Figure 3, creatinine and eGFR trends over time) and blood pressure remained stable, and no adverse effects were reported. Given his clinical improvement, advanced age, prior renal impairment, and low-normal blood pressure, a risk-benefit assessment supported maintaining vericiguat at the low dose.

In May 2024, due to repeated episodes of CHF exacerbation, vericiguat was initiated at 2.5 mg once daily. At the time of initiation, he had a low-normal systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 105 mmHg and a normal heart rate. Renal function and blood pressure were monitored every 2-4 weeks during follow-up. After three months of therapy, he demonstrated marked clinical improvement, with resolution of dyspnea and only mild leg swelling noted. He had no further hospitalizations during this period, and repeat TTE showed an increase in LVEF to 30%. Renal function (Figure 3, creatinine and eGFR trends over time) and blood pressure remained stable, and no adverse effects were reported. Given his clinical improvement, advanced age, prior renal impairment, and low-normal blood pressure, a risk-benefit assessment supported maintaining vericiguat at the low dose.

summary.text: A 78-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, GERD and BPH was evaluated for atrial flutter in October 2021 after prior-week chest discomfort. He was frail with limited strenuous-task capacity but no cognitive impairment. Initial LVEF was 50–55%; apixaban and metoprolol were started. Further evaluation was planned, but overseas travel was followed by loss to follow-up.

He returned in March 2022 after decompensated-HF admissions, with atrial fibrillation, global LV hypokinesis, 20–25% EF, NYHA II chronic systolic HFrEF, and mild-to-moderate CAD treated medically. The abstract attributes HF to ischemic cardiomyopathy. His home-country medications were revised and dapagliflozin was added.

LVEF improved to 30% and NYHA I by July 2023, followed by renal decline/hyperkalemia, spironolactone withdrawal and replacement of rivaroxaban with apixaban. Later dyspnea and significant leg swelling progressed to NYHA III; intensified diuretics and spironolactone reintroduction did not prevent recurrent admissions. EF reached 15–20% by February 2024.

Vericiguat 2.5 mg daily was started in May 2024 with BP/renal monitoring every 2–4 weeks. After three months, dyspnea resolved, leg swelling was mild, EF was 30% and NYHA I, and no further admissions, hypotension, electrolyte abnormalities or other adverse effects were reported; renal function/BP stayed stable. Escalation was avoided because of age, CKD, low-normal BP and prior MRA-associated hyperkalemia. Authors describe a temporal association and cannot establish vericiguat causality.
